body.statement:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field and let \((V_i)_{i\in D}\) be a finite family of subspaces.  There are vectors \(v_i\in V_i\), one for every \(i\in D\), which are linearly independent if and only if
\[
\dim\left(\sum_{i\in I}V_i\right)\ge |I|
\quad\text{for every }I\subseteq D.
\]

source.locator: Theorem 1, specialized to the vector matroid
source.verbatim_statement: if no group of k of the sets A_i is contained in a sub-space of k−1 dimensions

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 1 in the Internet Archive scan of The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics, volume 13 (1942), pages 83–89; the preceding paragraph states Hall-type necessity and Theorem 1 gives sufficiency for linear independence.
